Content: Mitosis and meiosis are `text(two)` processes that can produce new cells in an organism. Which statement correctly compares and contrasts the new cells produced by `text(each process)`?

D.Choice: New cells produced by mitosis maintain genetically identical offspring, and new cells produced by meiosis contribute to genetic diversity in offspring.

Content: Under ideal circumstances in an environment, a population will grow exponentially. However, in studies of actual populations in various environments, scientists have found that the exponential growth rate a population may experience for a while will slow down and may eventually level off at a constant rate. This is called logistic growth.
problems/MS23HSB/media/9a.jpg
problems/MS23HSB/media/9b.jpg
Which factor would `text(most likely)` cause the growth rate of a population to shift from exponential to logistic growth?

A.Choice: Predators that hunt the population are eliminated due to disease.

B.Choice: The birth rate in the population exceeds the death rate in the population.

C.Choice: The population consumes food resources as fast as they can be produced.

D.Choice: A competing population migrates to another area, leaving an excess of food and space.

Content: Ensatina is a genus of salamander present along the `text(western)` coast of North America. This salamander is thought to have started in the wet environments of `text(northern)` California and `text(southern)` Oregon (Oregon ensatina). From this location, the salamanders moved `text(northward)` into similar wet environments and `text(southward)` into much drier environments. Over time, some of the salamanders reached `text(northern)` Mexico. The map shows the locations of different subspecies of Ensatina.
problems/MS23HSB/media/15a.jpg
Which statement `text(best)` describes the ensatina salamanders?

A.Choice: The `text(southern)` movement of ensatinas resulted in salamanders that became more similar, resulting in multiple subspecies becoming a `text(single)` subspecies.

B.Choice: The `text(northern)` movement of ensatinas resulted in a new subspecies of the salamander that was able to survive in new and different environments.

C.Choice: The `text(northern)` movement of ensatinas resulted in salamanders that were less similar as their environments became drier and hotter.

D.Choice: The `text(southern)` movement of ensatinas into drier, warmer environments that had less similar salamanders resulted in a `text(single)` subspecies becoming at least `text(two)` different subspecies.

Content: Tapeworms attach themselves to the inner surface of the intestine in cows and consume some of the passing food material before the cow can obtain the material's nutrients. Which statement `text(best)` explains the role the tapeworm plays in relation to the cow?

A.Choice: The tapeworm is a predator because it lives inside of and attacks the cow.

B.Choice: The tapeworm is a competitor because it consumes nutrients the cow consumes.

C.Choice: The tapeworm is a commensalist because it cannot survive without a cow host to protect it.

D.Choice: The tapeworm is a parasite because it benefits from living inside the cow and harms the cow.

A student purchased a geranium plant from a greenhouse. The student uses the materials listed below to transfer the geranium plant to a new container.

:ibox:`bbtext(Materials)`

• `4text(,)000` `text(grams)` potting soil
• `5` `text(grams)` fertilizer (contains nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium)
• `1` large clay flowerpot
• `1` mature geranium plant
• `1text(,)000` `text(milliliters)` water
• `2` worms
Which criterion and reasoning work together to correctly classify a material from the list as living or nonliving?

A.Choice:
`bbtext(Criterion)`: Living things have mass and volume, and nonliving things do not.
`bbtext(Reasoning)`: Since the soil has mass and volume, the soil is living.

B.Choice:
`bbtext(Criterion)`: Nonliving things absorb water, and living things do not.
`bbtext(Reasoning)`: Since the flowerpot cannot absorb water, the flowerpot is living.

C.Choice:
`bbtext(Criterion)`: Nonliving things reproduce, and living things do not.
`bbtext(Reasoning)`: Since the worms can produce offspring, the worms are living.

D.Choice:
`bbtext(Criterion)`: Living things require nutrients, and nonliving things do not.
`bbtext(Reasoning)`: Since the geranium plant uses the fertilizer to grow, the geranium plant is living.
